sections.html:
Germantown is an eastern suburb of Memphis in Shelby County, covering just under 20 square miles of land. The city grew on a ridge between the Wolf River and Nonconnah Creek, about 16 miles east of the Mississippi River. It has its own mayor-alderman government, with a mayor and five part-time aldermen elected to four-year terms, and a professional city administrator who handles daily operations.

Annual events include the Germantown Charity Horse Show in June and the Germantown Festival, an arts and crafts fair, in early September. The Arbor Day Foundation has named it a Tree City USA for 33 consecutive years.

In 2019 the city won the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award, and Wikipedia notes only five municipalities have ever received it. A seller's day-to-day contact with the city is more practical: tax statements, code compliance and a design review process for exterior changes.

sections.h2: How did Germantown get its name and its look?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived around 1825. The area was called Pea Ridge from 1833, town lots were laid out in 1834, and the name changed to Germantown in 1836 to reflect German families nearby. The town was chartered in 1841, and the Memphis and Charleston Railroad came through in 1852. Yellow fever epidemics between 1867 and 1878 cut the population roughly in half.

The name briefly changed to Neshoba, a Chickasaw word for wolf, from May 15, 1917 until April 4, 1922, during the anti-German feeling of World War I. Germantown became a city in 1959, and its population climbed from about 500 to just over 40,000 over the following decades while leaders used development rules and design controls to manage growth.

Old Germantown centers on the railroad depot on Germantown Road, rebuilt in 1948 to replace the 1868 original and now home to a train museum. Fort Germantown, off Poplar Pike, is on the National Register, and the John Gray House in Municipal Park predates 1851.

Germantown has leveled off. The Census Bureau counted 38,844 people in 2010 and 41,333 in 2020, and its July 2025 estimate is 40,001, which is 3.2 percent below the 2020 base. Land area is 19.99 square miles, and density was 2,068 people per square mile in 2020.

With 2,068 residents per square mile and a shrinking head count, Germantown is a city where houses change hands one at a time rather than in big new subdivisions.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Germantown homes?
sections.html:
Germantown is a city of homeowners. QuickFacts lists an owner-occupied rate of 86.7 percent, well above Franklin at 63.8 percent and Gallatin at 57.1 percent, with 15,568 households and 2.60 people per household. The median home value is $470,800 for 2020 to 2024. Median owner costs are $2,546 a month with a mortgage and $923 without one, and median gross rent is $1,816.

Median household income is $149,920, and 71.9 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Residents 65 and older make up 24.2 percent of the population, and 92.3 percent lived in the same house one year earlier.

sections.h2: Which school systems serve Germantown houses?
sections.html:
Germantown is served by two public systems, which matters when a buyer asks which school a given address feeds. The city runs its own Germantown Municipal School District, and three campuses inside the city limits remain with Shelby County Schools.

  • Germantown Municipal School District: Dogwood, Farmington and Forest Hill elementary schools, Riverdale K-8, Houston Middle School and Houston High School
  • Shelby County Schools: Germantown Elementary, Germantown Middle and Germantown High, an International Baccalaureate school
  • Private options: Evangelical Christian School, St. George's Independent School, The Bodine School, Our Lady of Perpetual Help and others

Because the two systems overlap, a seller should confirm the zoned school with the district before putting a line about it in a listing.

sections.h2: What does Germantown property tax cost and when is it due?
sections.html:
The city rate is $1.7825 per $100 of assessed value. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value, commercial at 40 percent and personal property at 30 percent. The Shelby County Assessor's Office does the valuations and gives the city a certified tax roll each October. Property tax produces about half of the revenue for city services.

Germantown property tax calendar (City of Germantown Finance)
WhenWhat happens
OctoberShelby County Assessor delivers the certified tax roll to the city
NovemberCity mails tax statements to owners or title holders
December 1Taxes are due and payable
Last day of FebruaryPostmark deadline to avoid state-mandated penalties and interest

The city is barred from giving relief on penalties. An owner who has not received a statement by early December can email Tax@Germantown-TN.gov or call 901-757-7218, and escrowed owners should pass the statement to their lender.

Shelby County sets its own appeal path. A request for an informal review at the assessor's office closes on the last day of May. The county Board of Equalization takes appeals from May 1 through June 30 with no filing fee, online or by mail, and a later step goes to the State Board of Equalization and then Shelby County Chancery Court. The 2026 filing window closed on June 30, 2026, and the board's page says it opens again each May 1.

sections.h2: What do code compliance and permits mean for a Germantown sale?
sections.html:
The Economic and Community Development Department, at 1920 S. Germantown Road, runs planning, public art and code compliance. Its Code Compliance officers enforce the Code of Ordinances, and the city publishes a residential ordinance guide covering noise, parking, pets and signs. Staff there also support the Planning, Design Review, Public Art and Economic Development commissions and the Board of Zoning Appeals. Property maintenance standards address landscaping, trash and exterior upkeep. Additions and fences need review under the city's project guidelines and permit process.

Before listing, call Code Compliance at 901-757-7281 and ask whether any open case is attached to the address. A sale can go smoothly or stall on that single question, and a seller who knows the answer can price the house with it in mind.

sections.h2: How is a Germantown deed recorded in Shelby County?
sections.html:
Germantown deeds are recorded by the Shelby County Register of Deeds, 1075 Mullins Station Road, Suite W165, Memphis, phone 901-222-8100. The office says a deed is usually recorded and mailed back in about one business day, with a digital copy online. Individuals cannot open an e-filing account on their own, and the office recommends a real estate professional who already has one. A quit claim deed typically costs about $12 to file.

If an owner has died without a probated will, the register notes that Tennessee requires one Affidavit of Heirship filed with its office, and that title companies often prefer three. Probate questions go to the Shelby County Probate Court Clerk at 901-222-3750.

The state's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of purchase price, paid by the grantee at recording, and the register collects it for the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: How many people live in Germantown, Tennessee?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 40,001 residents in July 2025, down from 41,333 in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: What is the Germantown property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city of Germantown rate is $1.7825 per $100 of assessed value. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When are Germantown property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due December 1, and payments must be postmarked by the last day of February to avoid state-mandated penalties. The city cannot waive those penalties.

faqs.q: What share of Germantown homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: About 86.7 percent, according to Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024. The median owner-occupied home value is $470,800.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a Germantown house?
faqs.a: The Shelby County Register of Deeds in Memphis records it. Call 901-222-8100, and expect the document back in about one business day.
